clinician.final_diagnosis: a ruptured renal AML two weeks after COVID-19 infection
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 22-year-old female with recent COVID-19 infection two weeks prior presented with acute-onset left flank pain radiating to the left shoulder. Laboratory tests revealed microhematuria and mild leukocytosis with normal coagulation profile. Abdominal CT without contrast demonstrated a left perirenal moderate volume hemorrhage with a fat dense lesion in the left kidney measuring 2.5 × 2.3 × 2.1 cm consistent with ruptured renal angiomyolipoma (AML). Interventional radiology performed embolization 12 hours after admission, with intraprocedural evaluation showing no aneurysmal dilation. Post-procedurally, the patient experienced continued hemorrhage and retroperitoneal hematoma, resulting in hemoglobin nadir of 6.8 g/dl requiring transfusion and supplemental oxygen due to diaphragmatic irritation. On hospital day 6, she developed respiratory COVID-19 symptoms and again tested positive by PCR. No follow-up imaging or final discharge status was documented.
